chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Being a woman in a man's world; publishers and repertoire
summary: She comments on the word 'standards' and how publishers handle new music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Yeah. So there's another thing, maybe I should have added it to that list of saying you're a woman in a man's world and all those other contrasts I was drawing before, but also this very fine line that you seem to have straddled in the course of your career between being a jazz singer and a pop singer. I mean, both in terms of the popularity of the appeal of what you do and also the, you know, the choice of content.

Well, what seems to be a dirty word among musicians and performers, you know, who really go in for the profession is commercialism. And we try not to be commercial, not that commercial wouldn't help but unless you happen to be a pop commercial singer you don't get an opportunity to introduce songs. You wind up having to wait until the top singers are done and then you wind up doing another version of it unless you wait say ten or fifteen years and do the song. Then it becomes an original version because as I said before, pop music from a commercial standpoint comes out it's usually submitted to the so-called top artists. And I don't know whether they have an arrangement with the

publishers to not release this music to anybody until after they have recorded it or what. But what you wind up being is just somebody whose plugging songs and you try to find material that suits you, number one, and you try to, if you got a hold of some of that music you would give your own version of it.

I have to make the comparison to, you know, what I used to do in the past with what I'm doing now. I think even among the musicians and the people I have an opportunity to work with, that there is maybe a little bit more appreciation for what I do now than in the past.
